title: Raidium
summary: Multi-tenant guild management SaaS for MMORPG communities, monetized through on-chain USDt payments on the Kaia blockchain.
description: A multi-tenant guild management platform I built alone for MMORPG communities. It tracks red boss spawns with Discord reminders, verifies attendance from screenshots via OCR, runs a points economy with weekly rankings, and hosts a marketplace with an auction system, all behind a 4-tier guild RBAC with complete per-guild data isolation. It serves 6+ guilds and is monetized through a 5-tier modular subscription ($3–$10 USDt/month) on the Kaia blockchain with automatic on-chain transaction verification, plus PayMongo for fiat. Since analytics went live in May 2026 it has drawn 16,700+ visitors from 76 countries (66,000+ pageviews), most of them through its public game tools and guides.
features: Red Boss tracking with spawn scheduling and Discord reminders through a QStash chain
Attendance system with screenshot verification via OCR
Points economy with weekly rankings and leaderboards
Marketplace with listing-based and auction system
Kaia USDt crypto payments (5-tier subscriptions with on-chain verification) plus PayMongo for fiat
Multi-tenancy with complete guild-scoped data isolation
4-tier RBAC with comprehensive audit logging
Self-hosted on my bare-metal server via Docker + Coolify
Android app with push notifications
Discord bot with slash commands and webhook alerts
Two-tier OCR: OCR.space first, then a self-hosted EasyOCR service I wrote
Public game tools and guides (relic calculator, class guides) that bring most of the traffic
GlitchTip error tracking, Umami analytics, and uptime checks on my own server

title: Operations platform for a real estate franchise
summary: Internal operations platform for a real estate franchise, and the public website that reads from it: offices, brokerage, agents, listings, transactions, and events in one system.
description: With a small team I build and run the internal operations platform of a real estate franchise, and the public website that reads from it. The platform is a Next.js app on Supabase/Postgres with a 9-role RBAC enforced in row-level security, a concurrency-safe commission engine, e-signature and document pipelines, and three-environment CI/CD with migration gates and integration tests. In October 2026 I moved the franchise off its old website builder and listings database in a single cutover: a read-only database role now feeds the new public site its listings, agents, and guides, with enquiries routed to the right agent, structured data, and every legacy URL carried over. Since then I have shipped a syndication feed to an international listings portal, foreclosure listings read from banks' PDF lists, event invitations with calendar files, and two-step verification on every password change. I am the top contributor by commits, and I merge every pull request the team lands, reviewing all of my teammates': 808 on the platform and 77 on the website so far.
features: 9-role RBAC enforced in Postgres row-level security
Concurrency-safe commission engine
E-signature and document pipelines
Public website fed by a read-only database role: listings, agents, guides, and enquiries
One-day cutover from the old website builder and listings database, legacy URLs and SEO intact
Listing syndication feed to an international portal, and shareable listing flyers with QR codes
Foreclosure listings parsed from banks' monthly PDF lists
Two-step verification on password changes, an enforced script policy, and monthly dependency audits
Three-environment CI/CD with migration gates and integration tests

title: My bare‑metal server
summary: One dedicated box that runs everything I ship: Raidium, its OCR service, the Pickleball GenSan backend, Nextmarket Sniper, and the monitoring, error tracking, analytics, and invoicing behind them.
description: A dedicated 8-core server with two SSDs in a RAID1 mirror, running Debian, that I set up in February 2026 and have run since. Coolify deploys my apps from a git push to main and builds them in Docker; NGINX and Certbot terminate TLS in front of 17 sites. Uptime Kuma, GlitchTip, and Umami are self-hosted on the same box, so I get uptime checks, Sentry-style error reports, and visitor analytics without paying a vendor. Freelance invoicing runs on InvoicePlane, which has no webhooks, so a small bash script on a systemd timer polls its database every 5 minutes and posts new payments into Sure, my finance tracker. SSH is key-only on a non-default port.
features: Coolify deploys from a git push: build, container, domain, and TLS in one step
NGINX reverse proxy with Certbot certificates in front of 17 sites
Self-hosted OCR microservice (FastAPI + EasyOCR) for Raidium's attendance screenshots
Uptime Kuma, GlitchTip (Sentry-compatible), and Umami, all self-hosted
InvoicePlane to Sure payment sync: a bash script on a 5-minute systemd timer
PostgreSQL, MariaDB, and Valkey behind the apps, with pgAdmin over them
Two SSDs in a RAID1 mirror
